summary: This Wikipedia article surveys the military history of the United States, from the Revolutionary War and the Northwest Indian War through the Civil War, the Spanish-American era reforms under Elihu Root, the Korean and Vietnam Wars, and World War II. It covers major campaigns, leaders, and turning points, and notes the postwar U.S. role as a superpower and its close defense ties with Britain.
one_line: Overview of U.S. military history from the Revolution and Indian wars through the Civil War, World Wars, Korea and Vietnam.
key_facts: The Battle of the Wabash in 1791 was the most severe defeat ever suffered by the United States at the hands of American Indians.
U.S. forces decisively defeated the Indian confederacy at the Battle of Fallen Timbers in 1794.
On April 12, 1861, Confederate forces opened fire on Fort Sumter, whose garrison was loyal to the Union.
A British army surrendered at Saratoga in 1777 after a sortie from Canada ended in disaster.
Secretary of War Elihu Root served from 1899 to 1904 and led the modernization of the Army.
Elihu Root's reforms helped establish the U.S. Army War College and the General Staff.
North Korean forces struck massively in the summer of 1950 and nearly drove US and ROK defenders into the sea.
MacArthur ordered an amphibious invasion at Inchon, cutting off and routing the North Koreans.
President Harry Truman fired Douglas MacArthur after disputes over the conduct of the Korean War.
An armistice in the Korean War was reached with the two Koreas remaining divided at the 38th parallel, and no peace treaty has been signed.
The Vietnam War was fought between 1959 and 1975, and major American military involvement began in 1964.
Congress gave President Lyndon B. Johnson blanket approval for presidential use of force in the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution.
Over 16 million Americans served in World War II, about 11% of the population, and over 400,000 died during the war.
The U.S. used atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, which quickly caused the surrender of Japan.
The U.S. Navy's aircraft carriers won a major victory over Japan at Midway just six months into the war.
